From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: FinServ - Post-call: data retention exception (PII in logs)

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- FinServ is evaluating Redwood for conversational assistants across regulated customer support flows.
- Primary ask: guarantee that PII captured in prompts or user messages will not be retained beyond a negotiated exception (0-retention) or be subject to a shortened retention schedule.
- Additional asks: data residency (US-only), customer-managed KMS, and demonstrable controls (SOC2, pen test).

What we can do / options to consider:
1) Zero-retention for PII fields: we can configure the ingestion pipeline to avoid persisting prompt text that is classified as PII. Operational metrics and non-PII metadata can remain for monitoring.
2) Shortened logs: maintain full logs for N days (e.g., 7) then purge; or keep indices without raw prompt content.
3) Client-side redaction/proxying: you can replace or hash PII before sending.
4) Data residency + encryption: we can run instances in a US-only region (us-east-1) and support CMK in KMS/HSM.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-request.pdf (form for exception) and SOC2-summary.pdf for your security team.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the formal retention exception you need (0-retention for prompt text vs 7-day shortened logs)?
- If 0-retention, I will loop in our Security and Legal leads to prepare an SOW/Security Appendix and proposed technical design.
- Suggest a follow-up with your security team Wed 3/17 10:00 AM ET — does that work?

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Rafael — thanks for the summary. Confirming our ask: FinServ requires a formal exception that ensures any PII captured in prompts or transcripts is not persisted in Redwood logs or storage (0-retention). We understand there are engineering patterns (proxy/redact) but for procurement and regulators we need contractual assurance and evidence that no raw prompt content containing PII is retained beyond processing.

Questions:
- Can you provide a written design that demonstrates the ingestion path and where content is persisted (or not)?
- Will your solution support US-only residency and CMK encryption?
- We will need SOC2 and penetration testing reports for our security review.

Procurement/legal will expect an SOW and security appendix they can sign via DocuSign once Security signs off.

— Elena
Elena Gomez
Head of Data Privacy | FinServ Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks for looping me in — Rafael, tagging a few internal notes and asks so we can move quickly: 

Internal checklist/actions (pre-Security/Legal review):
- Confirm feasibility: can we offer a configuration that results in no persisted prompt tokens for a customer (zero-retention mode)?
- Prepare a short technical design doc and operational runbook showing where data is kept, purge timing, and audit trail. (I attached internal-presales-checklist.pdf).
- Identify what telemetry/metrics we still need for observability if raw prompts are not retained.
- Confirm pagination/kv-cache implications for stateful sessions (we may need ephemeral session streaming with no disk-backed KV).

Options to propose to FinServ (quick):
A) Redwood-managed zero-retention for PII fields (we implement filters and no persistence of raw prompt text).
B) 7-day shortened logs: keep full logs for 7 days, then purge raw content and retain metadata only.
C) Customer-side redaction + standard logs (lowest risk).

Please loop in Security (neha_kapoor) and Legal (we'll request Legal review from Priyom) — I can own the presales design and draft the SOW appendix.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinServ - data retention exception (PII in logs)

Elena — appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can support a zero-retention design for PII with the caveats below. Attaching our initial design (redwood-0-retention-design.md) and linking our HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FS-2027-89.

Technical summary (proposed):
- Ingestion filtering: we will apply PII detection rules at the ingress layer. When text is flagged as PII, we will:
  * process the request in-memory for model inference,
  * avoid writing the raw prompt/transcript to persistent logs or object storage,
  * emit minimal anonymized telemetry (latency, token counts, non-identifying metadata).
- Session state: for customers requiring stateful behavior, we can use ephemeral session cache that is never checkpointed to disk; customers may optionally use client-side state storage.
- Audit/operational logs: we can provide an audit trail showing request ids and hashes but not raw prompt content.
- Data residency & encryption: we will provision in us-east-1 and support customer-managed KMS keys.

Next steps:
1) Security and Legal (Neha) to review the design and draft a security appendix for the SOW.
2) If accepted, our Legal team will prepare an SOW + DocuSign package.
3) Schedule the security deep-dive (proposed Wed 3/17 10:00 AM ET).

If you can send the formal exception request (finserv-data-retention-exception-request.docx) to procurement, we'll kick off internal sign-offs.

Thanks — Rafael

Elena
